name: 1726 Prairie Avenue: the two-storey brick building on the alley, K12

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on the 1911 sheet carried back seven years (the T-1840 census rules it present, census row s20-1726-r1, as the district draft did). Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws behind lots 5 and 6 (1726 and 1728 in its margin) a yellow, FRAME building about 6.6 m deep (columns 347.4-366.4) by 11.3 m along the alley (rows 1587.0-1619.7), starting about 2.8 m south of the lot 4/5 line, uncrossed, where the 1911 sheet draws this brick one (half-height edges of a yellow-density profile on the committed plate raster at its 0.346 m a pixel; docs/RESEARCH/k12-1726-stable-1932/robinson-1886-lots-5-6.jpg). So this building replaced the plate's frame one after 1886; nothing read here dates it more closely, and a building first seen in 1911, and lettered GARAGE there, may postdate 1904. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (west) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 20 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_20.jpg) at pixel (2224.98, 5415.74): the alley wall's line by median darkness profiles over rows 5300-5400 and 5450-5540 (peaks at columns 2224.94 and 2225.01), halfway between its north wall line (row 5277.09) and its south wall line (row 5554.39, on the 1726/1730 lot line, which the same profile east of the building finds at row 5554.80), each the peak of a median darkness profile over columns 2330-2430 and 2240-2420, peaks refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json): local E 1335.974, N -3164.259. The bearing is the parcel's and the neighbouring K12 stables' (walker_house_1720_prairie_coach_house, -0.581 degrees). The fit's own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed.
placement.symbolic_location: 1726 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: on the alley, its south wall on the 1726/1730 lot line, parcel prairie_1726 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 2224.98) to its east wall line (2454.62, a median darkness profile over rows 5290-5540) and from its north wall line (row 5277.09) to its south one (5554.39): 229.6 by 277.3 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 11.661 m deep by 14.081 m along the alley. The trace s20fp-1726-b2 also takes in a piece 4.07 m deep (east wall at column 2308.33) by 4.33 m (from the 1720/1726 lot line, row 5189.75, to this building's north wall) on the alley line north of it: the one-storey range that by 1911 ran on from 1720's stable to here, with no wall drawn across it on the lot line. It is not built for 1904 (see the research note).

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12 12' (inches, the first storey's and the second's, as the key reads them) inside its north wall and again inside its south wall on the lot line. Robinson's 1886 plate draws a frame building on this ground (see the phase's dates); the brick is the 1911 sheet's alone.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick, the fire-wall end and the sheet's window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1726-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 12', no stable's X (it letters the building GARAGE, a 1911 use not carried to 1904), the key's fire-wall sign with two ticks at the alley end of its north wall and of its south wall, and one of the key's window marks, on the alley wall about 7.51 m from the north wall line and 6.57 m from the south, with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there). The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (`mirror`): its party wall stands at the south end, on the 1726/1730 lot line, against the two-storey piece of 1730's alley building whose north wall the sheet draws on the same line; its open gable at the north end, which faces the 4.3 m of open ground between it and the end of 1720's range, and carries no opening, as the sheet marks none. The sheet's fire-wall sign at the north end is not built: the kit has one party wall and one open gable. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley wall's from the south end, the yard wall's from the north end, as the kit lays them in mirror image). The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 6.24). The carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the south end, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the north end, are the kit's. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between four stable sash, with loft sash over the outer two. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees over the 11.66 m span, as the deep stables (1616, 1612, 1626, 1628, 1700, 1720, 1736) took, about 3.4 m from eave to ridge. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the sheet's solid dot inside the building about 1 m from its south wall and 1 m from its east wall, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none), and the 1911 range piece north of the building (see the record's research note). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the 1726 house's rear wall line, 10.79 m east of the yard wall.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot with the sheet's window mark where it puts them, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 20 of the 1911 Sanborn draws a two-storey brick building on the alley behind 1726, uncrossed, and letters it GARAGE. GARAGE is a 1911 use and is not read as the 1904 one (the K12 kit's restriction no_1911_use_labels; T-1837 study ruling 11; the T-1840 census: 'carried as a 1904 service building of unread use, not as a garage', s20-1726-r1). This record builds it as the house's stable and coach house, as 1736's GARAGE is (T-2995): a carriage bay, a loft with its hatch and hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. The use is RECONSTRUCTED; no source names a horse, a carriage or a motor car on this lot, and Robinson's 1886 plate stands a frame building here, not this one (see the phase's dates).

research_note: T-1932 refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit. The sheet census (census row s20-1726-r1, trace s20fp-1726-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. The two-storey building is 14.08 m along the alley by 11.66 m deep, its south wall on the 1726/1730 lot line, against the two-storey piece of 1730's alley building. The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (as 1612's is): its party wall at the south end on the lot line, its open gable to the north. The sheet's one window mark, on the alley wall 7.51 m from its north wall line, is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it. The trace also takes in, north of the building, a 4.07 by 4.33 m piece of the one-storey brick range that by 1911 joined 1720's stable range to this building across the 1720/1726 lot line, with no wall drawn on the line; that piece is NOT built for 1904. Robinson's 1886 plate ends 1720's range on the lot line and stands a frame building, not a brick one, behind lots 5 and 6, and 1720's record (L-k12-1720-stable-range-1932) builds the range ending on the line with a closed end wall, as the plate ends it. No picture of it is known. The reading is in docs/RESEARCH/k12-1726-stable-1932/README.md.
